items.item_text: California Licensed Pharmacy Technician
Pharmacy Technician Certification (CPhT) from the Pharmacy Technician Certification Board (PTCB)
Minimum education satisfied through attainment of the required licensure/certification
Two (2) years of working experience as a licensed Pharmacy Technician in an outpatient (retail or specialty) pharmacy setting
Experience typing prescriptions into a pharmacy processing system
Experience in Health System Outpatient Pharmacy
Experience resolving prescription adjudication rejections with insurance companies
Experience working in a Specialty Pharmacy
Experience in chart review and working with health insurance companies
Prior Authorization or Patient Assistance Program experience in Epic EMR, Willow Ambulatory, specialty pharmacy case management systems or other clinical software
Experience with generic and trade drug names and pharmacy terminology
Experience in MS Office suite: Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access

Experience ensuring compliance of specialty pharmacy accrediting bodies [e.g., Utilization Review Accreditation Commission (URAC), The Joint Commission (TJC), Accreditation Commission of Health Care (ACHC), etc.]
Experience working for a Pharmacy Benefit Management company
Experience submitting and following up on prior authorizations and appeals
Experience navigating copay and financial assistance (patient assistance) programs and applications

The Pharmacy Technician Specialist is responsible for gathering information from medical records and other sources as required to process prior authorizations, patient assistance requests, and other ancillary tasks related to the operation of a Specialty Pharmacy program. Makes analysis of what further information needs to be collected to complete patient history. Makes recommendations to Pharmacist based on protocols and data gathered. Communicates authorization requests to requesting parties. Assists with processing of prior authorization and patient assistance program requests. Maintains database of activities to document workload and impact on patient outcomes. #CA-DS
40% - Prior Authorizations and Patient Assistance Programs
25% - Participates in Chart Review Process and Clinical Assessment Preparation and Refill Reminders/Adherence Calls to Patients
15% - Works with Clinical Pharmacist to provide patient care
5% - Prescription Filling
5% - Completes documentation on all requests
5% - Follows protocol/policy to make recommendations to the Pharmacist
5% - Follows up with Medical Personnel and/or Pharmacy
Familiarity with electronic methods of communication, (i.e., email, computer messaging)
Recent knowledge of Pharmacy Dispensing Software and Third-Party Billing
Ability to be self-motivated and work with minimal supervision yet to recognize when it is appropriate to seek assistance from others when limits of authority have been reached
Ability to communicate clearly with patients and hospital personnel, both orally and in writing
Knowledge of hospital, department and university policies and procedures
Ability to make decisions about when to request more information in order to complete a full medical history
Ability to be a self-starter in a new clinic environment
Ability to communicate prescription authorizations to pharmacists, medical personnel, or pharmacies
Knowledge of generic and trade drug names and pharmacy terminology
Ability to use pharmacy information systems and look-up patient data on hospital information systems
Ability to operate fax machine, photocopier and voice mail system
Ability to use an electronic medical record (EMR)
Ability to use spreadsheet and word-processing programs

Interpersonal skills to establish and maintain a friendly, welcoming environment for clinic’s/department’s customers, to demonstrate an interested, understanding, compassionate manner, to maintain a courteous and calm demeanor, and to use a proactive approach to negotiate with and persuade others to take required action

Ability to maintain composure, efficiency and a positive, customer-service oriented manner during periods of peak workload, with frequent interruptions, under tight deadlines, and when interacting with challenging customers who may be ill, angry or emotionally distressed

Problem-solving skills to independently recognize and define a problem and identify the resources available to help solve the problem, create and implement viable solutions, and follow through to ensure the problem is resolved to the satisfaction of all parties
Working knowledge of current California Pharmacy Law
